categories_thin: Roofing, siding and windows: only about six firms are actually based in New Brunswick; almost every siding/window contractor serving the city is headquartered in East Brunswick, Edison, North Brunswick or South Plainfield.
Pest control: only two New Brunswick phone numbers were findable, and neither publishes a street address.
Locksmiths: the two entries are city-name websites that may be dispatch networks rather than local shops.
Pools: virtually all pool companies covering New Brunswick are based elsewhere; only International Swimming Pools and Elite Lawn Sprinklers have in-city addresses.
Moving and storage: in-city options are mostly national self-storage chains (excluded) plus a couple of broker-style listings; only one small local mover was found.

Restoration and water damage: the New Brunswick-branded providers (SERVPRO, Roto-Rooter, Paul Davis, PuroClean) are franchises or national brands and were excluded, leaving only a mold specialist and two waterproofing firms.
Cleaning: many results were national cleaning brands or individual cleaners without a business address; only a few qualifying local firms were confirmed.
caveats: Zone is the City of New Brunswick. Contractors based in North Brunswick, East Brunswick, Highland Park, Milltown, Somerset or Edison that merely serve New Brunswick were excluded unless they list a New Brunswick street address.
The 118-120 Sandford St and 1100 Somerset St industrial buildings house many one-bay body/repair shops with unit numbers; several may share owners or be dormant. Cross-check before outreach.
Auto-body entries taken from the NJ MVC licensed facility PDF are state-licensed but may have no web presence; 'active_evidence' reflects the licence list, not recent reviews.

A cluster of contractor 'brands' (NJ Commercial and Industrial Roofing, Castlestone Paving, Princeton Electrical Makeover) all list 317 George St Suite 320 - this looks like a shared office or marketing set-up and should be verified as separate operating businesses.
Several contractor addresses are filing addresses (apartments or homes) rather than staffed offices, which is normal for small trades but means in-person visits may not be possible.
Some review counts (e.g., Everest Driveways 395, T&J Stone 122) look large for a small local firm and may reflect aggregated or incentivised reviews.
data_gaps: OpenStreetMap/Overpass API returned HTTP 406 from this environment, so no OSM cross-check was possible.

Yellow Pages, Yelp, BBB, Superpages, Manta, ChamberofCommerce.com, Cylex, AllPages and ShowMeLocal block direct page fetches (HTTP 403); their content was read only through search-result snippets, so some entries could not be verified in depth.
Birdeye pages 6 and 7 of the New Brunswick contractors directory (listings roughly 51-70) returned truncated content, so about a dozen entries in that range were missed.
Google Maps served a limited view (about five results per query) and the shared browser session was contended by other research sessions, limiting map-based enumeration.
The City of New Brunswick publishes no reachable online business-licence directory; only the French Street/Joyce Kilmer corridor directory was available.
Phone numbers are missing for many small shops whose directories omit them; the triage team should pull them from map listings.
